A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 47-page versions of the same WCDE study. Page-by-page text and visual comparisons support matching the main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original WCDE simulation results, including variance and MSE on synthetic DAGs and the ASIA, SIGNALING, and MILDEW networks.

after.justification: The original simulation studies remain, with revised MILDEW results in Tables D.2 and D.3.

M1.justification: The proposed WCDE adjustment criterion, O-set construction, and AIPW estimator in Equation 5.1 are unchanged. The revised MILDEW filtering description concerns selection of experimental comparison sets.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic DAGs and ASIA, SIGNALING, and MILDEW networks, with unchanged treatment–outcome pairs and estimation tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2 reports a MILDEW comparison pool of 122 valid adjustment sets instead of 112. This changes the pool of alternative adjustment strategies evaluated, without introducing a new estimator family. The displayed top-50 tables do not identify the complete membership difference.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 changes candidate filtering from the backdoor criterion to the adjustment criterion. This is a reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish whether it reflects rerunning experiments or correcting their description. Sample sizes and variance/MSE metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The variable-addition and pruning checks supporting Lemmas 4.4–4.7, including Table 2, are unchanged. The MILDEW revision updates existing benchmark comparisons without introducing a new ablation, robustness scenario, error analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: Reporting practices are unchanged, including Appendix D.1's 50 random coefficient configurations and 100 Monte Carlo replications. Revised empirical variance values do not establish a change in uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: MILDEW values and rankings change throughout Tables D.2–D.3, including one replacement in the displayed top-50 membership. For the O-set at n = 500, variance/MSE changes from 0.00280/0.00283 to 0.00269/0.00269. Section 5 changes the claimed best-performance threshold from n >= 1000 to n >= 500, although v4 Table D.3 contradicts the latter. Other benchmark results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 removes the blanket assertion that RAL estimators are unbiased, a limited correction to their mathematical characterization. The formal definitions, identification and optimality theorems, influence-function expressions, and appendix proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same contributions concerning WCDE identification, influence functions, optimal adjustment, and efficient estimation. The changed MILDEW threshold is a localized experimental claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of mediator–confounder interactions and qualifications concerning asymptotic guarantees, known DAGs, and causal-discovery errors are unchanged. The altered MILDEW threshold reports a different finding without adding a mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: The MILDEW reproduction instructions revise the candidate-filtering criterion and resulting set count in Appendix D.2. Estimator implementation details, hyperparameters, synthetic data-generation instructions, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to CDE, ATE adjustment, and causal-discovery research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits include the RAL description, MILDEW reporting, and the change from 'consistent with G' to 'consistently with G' in Appendix B.1. The version stamp changes, but section organization and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table D.2 corrects the malformed m1,2 label to m, adjusts column spacing, and swaps its final two rows. Table D.3 reorders the displayed sets. The figure and table inventory, captions, and placement are retained.

improvement.justification: The RAL wording correction and repaired table label improve precision, but v4 introduces an unsupported empirical summary. V3's n >= 1000 MILDEW statement agrees with the displayed results; v4 claims n >= 500, although Table D.3 gives [m1,m2,k2,k] variance/MSE of 0.00244/0.00245 versus the O-set's 0.00269/0.00269 at n = 500. This weakens agreement between the narrative and evidence. The deterioration is limited because the core formal results and other experiments remain unchanged.
